tau_strictly_decreases_aux.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite additive commutative group, equipped with a $\sigma$-algebra in which every singleton is measurable, and suppose $G$ carries a module structure over $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$. Let $\Omega_{01}$ and $\Omega_{02}$ be measure spaces whose canonical measures $\mathbb{P}_{01}$, $\mathbb{P}_{02}$ are probability measures, and let $\Omega$ be a measure space whose canonical measure $\mathbb{P}$ is a probability measure. Let $p$ be a reference package (`refPackage Ω₀₁ Ω₀₂ G`), i.e. the data of measurable maps $X^0_1:\Omega_{01}\to G$, $X^0_2:\Omega_{02}\to G$ and a real number $\eta=p.\eta$ with $0<\eta$ and $8\eta\le 1$.

Notation. For a measurable space $S$, a measure $m$ on $S$ and a map $Z:\Omega'\to S$ from a measurable space $\Omega'$ with measure $\mu$, the entropy is $H[Z;\mu]=H(Z_*\mu)$, where for a measure $m$ on $S$, $H(m)=\sum_{s\in S} -\,m'(\{s\})\log m'(\{s\})$ with $m'=m(S)^{-1}m$ (i.e. $\sum_s \phi(m'(\{s\}))$ with $\phi(t)=-t\log t$). For $Y_1:\Omega_1\to G$ with measure $\mu_1$ on $\Omega_1$ and $Y_2:\Omega_2\to G$ with measure $\mu_2$ on $\Omega_2$, the Ruzsa distance is $d[Y_1;\mu_1\,\#\,Y_2;\mu_2]=H\big(\pi_*((Y_1)_*\mu_1\otimes(Y_2)_*\mu_2)\big)-\tfrac12H[Y_1;\mu_1]-\tfrac12H[Y_2;\mu_2]$, where $\pi(x,y)=x-y$ on $G\times G$. The $\tau$-functional is $\tau[Y_1;\mu_1\,\#\,Y_2;\mu_2\mid p]=d[Y_1;\mu_1\,\#\,Y_2;\mu_2]+\eta\, d[X^0_1;\mathbb{P}_{01}\,\#\,Y_1;\mu_1]+\eta\, d[X^0_2;\mathbb{P}_{02}\,\#\,Y_2;\mu_2]$.

Let $X_1,X_2,X_1',X_2':\Omega\to G$ be measurable maps such that $X_1'$ has the same distribution under $\mathbb{P}$ as $X_1$, $X_2'$ has the same distribution under $\mathbb{P}$ as $X_2$, and the four maps $X_1,X_2,X_1',X_2'$ are jointly independent under $\mathbb{P}$. Assume that $(X_1,X_2)$ minimizes $\tau$ in the sense of `TauMinimizes p X₁ X₂`: for all probability measures $\nu_1,\nu_2$ on $G$, $\tau[X_1;\mathbb{P}\,\#\,X_2;\mathbb{P}\mid p]\le\tau[\mathrm{id};\nu_1\,\#\,\mathrm{id};\nu_2\mid p]$, where $\mathrm{id}:G\to G$ is the identity. If $\eta=1/9$, then $d[X_1;\mathbb{P}\,\#\,X_2;\mathbb{P}]=0$.
